NextItNet’s endpoint depends on causal convolution paths: receptive-field span R = 1 + Σℓ(kℓ−1)dℓ for stride-one layers, counting every convolution; exact reachable offsets can contain holes. Original residual blocks use convolutions at d and 2d, while bottleneck blocks use one temporal convolution. Deleting and compacting history changes item lags and potentially receptive-field membership. With left padding, read the final nonpadding position, never count−1. [Paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [author implementation](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet/blob/master/ops.py).

Implementation-derived implications: channel-only LayerNorm preserves temporal locality; normalization across time can introduce length dependence and dependencies beyond the convolutional field. Zero padding embeddings alone do not guarantee padding invariance: learned convolution biases and LayerNorm offsets can create nonzero padding states that propagate forward. Extra explicit left padding can therefore differ from implicit per-layer boundary zeros. Consistent masking of padding states at intermediate operations can restore invariance; verify the actual operation order. Prefix changes outside the exact endpoint receptive field should have no effect under purely local operations. [Normalization, biases and padding code](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html).

Suggested matched controls: compare oldest-prefix deletion with equal-count random/interior deletions while holding the recent suffix fixed; compare compaction with position-preserving zero replacement to separate lag changes from content removal. Replace old items with matched alternative items at identical positions to preserve length and boundary geometry. Shuffle only the old prefix, preserving its items and recent suffix, to test order. Separately vary explicit left-padding width while preserving history and endpoint-relative lags. Use eval mode, identical candidates and paired users. Improvements after deletion alone cannot establish stale-history interference; require corroborating fixed-geometry content controls.
